text:
B: Hi! Hello, can you hear me?
A: Yeah. Hiya.
B: Hi, I'm Elira. Sorry, I always do that, I always start talking straight away. How was your last one?
A: Fine. He were alright. We argued about bread rolls mostly.
B: Bread rolls? Oh no, the barm thing? I've heard about that.
A: The barm thing, yeah. He's wrong, anyway.
B: Ha. Erm, so what do you do? Sorry, is that boring, everyone's going to ask that.
A: It's fine. Software developer. I look after a payroll system, councils and NHS trusts use it.
B: Oh, payroll! Okay, that's actually so useful, I'm doing a bookkeeping course at the minute, AAT, and we've just started the payroll bits and I'm sort of drowning in it. Like, tax codes. What even is an emergency tax code?
A: Erm. It's what they put you on when they don't know enough about you yet. Usually you've started a new job and there's no P45, so you get the basic allowance with no history. It's on a non-cumulative basis, so each pay period's worked out on its own. You'd normally see a W1 or an M1 after the code. Then it sorts itself out once HMRC send the right one through, and you get the overpaid tax back.
B: Oh my God, that's the clearest anyone's ever explained it. The course just says "see section four".
A: Courses are always like that.
B: Are you doing one as well?
A: I've started a couple. Work pays for them. I never finish the coursework, do you know what I mean.
B: Honestly, same, I've got about six tabs open of modules I haven't done. I'm between jobs right now, so I've got no excuse really.
A: Right. What happened?
B: Redundancy. Voluntary. They restructured and merged my role with someone else's, so, erm, I sort of took the money. It wasn't my fault, but it still feels a bit embarrassing, you know? Telling people.
A: It's not embarrassing.
B: No, I know.
A: They're talking about replacing our whole system. Cloud migration. So I'll probably be in the same boat.
B: Oh no, really? But surely they'd need you, if you're the one who knows how it works?
A: That's what I tell myself.
B: Sorry, I didn't mean to, erm, bring it up.
A: You didn't, I did.
B: Ha, fair. Okay, happier thing. You've got a dog, right? I saw the lead in your photo.
A: Yeah. Bramble. Cocker spaniel. She ate a whole loaf off the side on Tuesday, bag and everything.
B: The bag as well?
A: Most of it. She was fine. I was googling at midnight, mind.
B: We keep saying we'll get a cat, me and my boyfriend, but our flat's tiny. There's a neighbour's cat that sits on our windowsill, so we just sort of borrow that one.
A: That's the best way. No vet bills.
B: Exactly! What do you have for dinner when you've had a long day? I'm always nosy about that.
A: For tea? My husband cooks, mostly. Chilli or something. Chippy on a Friday.
B: Tea, sorry, yeah. Chippy Friday is so good, though.
